description: Machine-readable Green Goods ontology: canonical entities, controlled vocabularies with per-layer representations, EAS schemas, cross-layer constraints, and lifecycle state machines. scripts/quality/check-ontology.mjs (bun run check:ontology) drift-gates every section against the code and docs anchors declared inline; bun run ontology:generate renders docs/docs/reference/ontology.generated.mdx and docs/docs/builders/integrations/entity-matrix.mdx from it. Entity and persona prose stays human-canonical in docs/docs/reference/glossary-community.md — this file mirrors it and the checker locks the two together. Maturity lives in the `capabilities` projection (implementation / deployment / activation / indexing / availability, each with evidence and verified_at); the per-item `status` field is only the drift-gate's code-crosscheck switch (live = representations checked, spec = planned-anchor watched), never a product-availability claim. Human explainers live in `concept_cards`; public claims live in packages/shared/src/ontology/marketing-claims.json.

excluded_from_v1: Impact-axes taxonomy — canon is maintained outside the repo; this public file carries only the four production action domains.
ModuleDependency and ModuleSchemaKind from the commitment-pooling spec — module wiring plumbing, not domain vocabulary.

personas.definition: A person doing regenerative Work in a garden. Submits Work, holds gardener Hats, receives credit toward Hypercerts and yield splits.

A local resident affected by a Garden's Work. Signals or attests that Work exists and is healthy, and helps prioritize future Actions through public signal and conviction flows.

constraints.statement: Action domains form a closed four-member set; resolvers reject domain values above 3 and garden domain masks are validated as 4-bit.
A Work attestation's attester must be a gardener or operator of the recipient garden, and the referenced action must exist, be started, not be expired, and belong to a domain enabled on that garden.
Only an operator of the garden may attest a Work Approval, and the approval's actionUID and recipient must match the referenced Work attestation.
The approver and the work attester must be different accounts — self-approval reverts.
An Assessment attester must be an evaluator or operator of the recipient garden.
The three-way yield split (CookieJar / Hypercert fractions / Juicebox) must sum to exactly 10000 bps.
Garden NFT transfers obey the TransferRestriction mode (Unrestricted / OwnerOnly / Locked); minting is always allowed.
Each core resolver validates that incoming attestations use its pinned schema UID.

holes.statement: Schema validation is skipped while the stored schemaUID is zero (the deployment window) — a documented gap the commitment-pooling spec explicitly refuses to inherit (its module deploys fail-closed).

constraints.statement: The six-role allocation snapshot stored at cycle open must sum to exactly 10000 bps and is immutable for the cycle.

Every member of a commitment's accountable lead/contributor team is excluded from every fulfillment-confirmation path, including the steward fallback; confirmation defaults are direction-aware (Offer → recipient, Request → creator).

The gardener-class recognition budget is fully allocated only after every fulfilled commitment has an eligible contributor: equal budget per fulfilled commitment, then the immutable cycle-open RecognitionPolicy allocates its equal-participation and verified-contribution components through separate deterministic remainder passes before the row results are added. The protocol default and immutable cycle-less preset are 20% equal / 80% verified, but an opened cycle may select any two values summing to 10000 bps. Zero eligible contributors block certificate expansion; there is no lead fallback.

An explicitly finalized commitment payout plan conserves the declared support amount exactly: garden-retained amount plus all contributor child amounts equals the parent amount. A zero-child all-retained plan completes at finalization without a transfer.

Each fulfilled commitment has at most one stable payout-plan pointer. The complete recognition vector matches its snapshot hash, payment weights derive from the atomic amount vector, finalization precedes dispatch, and child or batch cancellation never clears the parent pointer.
A pool may have at most one open Season at a time (O(1) openSeasonCycleId guard); Campaigns may overlap freely.
CommitmentRegistry unit classes are non-transferable by construction — no transfer, approval, or custody surface; balances move only via the module.

All four Needs schemas use EAS recipient as the canonical garden and expirationTime zero; a Need is a root with refUID zero, while NeedSignal, NeedStatus, and FundingAttribution use refUID to reference an exact live same-garden Need.

For each Need and attester, readers first select the greatest unsigned (timeCreated, uid) NeedSignal tuple and then apply revocation and expiry; a revoked or expired winner clears the signal without restoring an older record, and support and non-support remain separate counts.

Exactly four Needs schemas route through two resolvers: NeedsResolver accepts only Need, NeedSignal, and NeedStatus with schema-specific Community or Operator authorization, while the ungated FundingAttribution schema routes through FundingAttributionResolver; unknown schema branches fail closed.

state_machines.note: Direction-aware fulfillment: the party receiving the team's work confirms by default (Offer → receiver, Request → creator), or a named group may be set before acceptance. A current local-garden steward/owner may use PoolFallback. When explicitly selected before acceptance and no ordinary/local confirmer is reachable, a current steward/owner of the registered Green Goods protocol garden may use ProtocolFallback. The authority paths are not time-based; module ownership alone grants neither fallback; every lead/contributor is excluded. Evidence/Work credit records only while Accepted and unfrozen; the contributor roster and credit ledger freeze atomically on the transition to ReadyForConfirmation or before a direct Fulfilled dispute resolution; Ready requires pre-freeze totalVerifiedCredits > 0 and a structurally reachable confirmer, while recognition additionally requires Fulfilled plus an opened cycle policy or the immutable cycle-less 20/80 default; disputes restore an explicitly stored prior state. Readiness gate (all paths): automatic once every repeatable action requirement is met and any declared assessment is attached; submitForConfirmation for evidence-only types requires evidenceCount ≥ 1; steward markReadyForConfirmation carries a reason. Every path requires an Open cycle when scoped (or the immutable cycle-less 20/80 policy), pre-freeze totalVerifiedCredits > 0, and either a reachable ordinary confirmer or an explicitly selected registered protocol-garden fallback; the contributor roster and credit ledger freeze atomically before the ready event. Dispute resolution: RestorePrevious replays the stored preDisputeState; an Expired prior state can never resolve Fulfilled.

known_issues.statement: v1-0.mdx §16.1 defines a "Report" entity (aggregated bundle of approved work for grants/Hypercert minting) that is absent from the canonical entity set, the ERD, and the code. Formalize or retire the term when the reporting feature is actually designed — it overlaps Hypercert bundling today.

The ERD's GardenAssessment shape lists only notes and mediaURIs, while the shipped assessment carries the full strategy kernel (domain, diagnosis, SMART outcomes, selected action UIDs, reporting period, assessmentConfigCID).
No runtime mapping function exists between the numeric Capital enum and the lowercase CapitalType union; index-based bridges are unsafe because the two declared orders currently differ.

concept_cards.why_it_matters: The home unit of Green Goods — a real community in a real place, with its own treasury, roles, and record.
concept_cards.example: TAS HUB in Awka, Nigeria documents solar and education work as one garden.

not_confused_with.reason: a garden may open exactly one commitment pool; the pool is a ledger inside the garden, not the garden itself

concept_cards.safe_claim: Gardens are live on Arbitrum One with Season One communities operating today.

concept_cards.why_it_matters: The menu of documentable work — each action defines what evidence counts before anyone submits.
concept_cards.example: “Plant native species” with photo evidence and a species count.

not_confused_with.reason: an Action is the template; Work is one documented instance of it

concept_cards.safe_claim: The action registry is live; gardens choose which actions are open for submissions.

concept_cards.why_it_matters: The atomic unit of proof: field evidence that becomes an on-chain record at submission — or the moment it syncs, when captured offline.
concept_cards.example: Twelve seedlings planted, three photos, submitted from an offline queue when signal returned.

not_confused_with.reason: Work documents what happened; a commitment records a promise that work will happen

concept_cards.safe_claim: Work is attested on-chain at submission; operator approval adds a separate linked approval record.

concept_cards.why_it_matters: The up-front baseline and strategy that frames a season of work before it begins — success criteria first, work second.
concept_cards.example: An evaluator sets a waste-domain baseline with three SMART outcomes for the quarter.

not_confused_with.reason: an assessment frames future work; it is explicitly not a review of submitted Work (that is Work Approval)

concept_cards.safe_claim: Assessments are live; evaluators and operators author them before work begins.

concept_cards.why_it_matters: Bundles a period of approved work into a fundable certificate, so finished work can attract support.
concept_cards.example: A season of approved agroforestry work minted as one certificate with contributor shares.

not_confused_with.reason: attestations are the raw records; a hypercert is a curated bundle of them

concept_cards.safe_claim: Operators mint impact certificates from approved work on Arbitrum today.

concept_cards.why_it_matters: Lets funders endow a garden: principal stays put while generated yield funds operations.
concept_cards.example: A funder deposits into a garden's vault; the garden harvests the yield each period.

not_confused_with.reason: vaults hold endowment principal; cookie jars hold small operational funds for frequent withdrawals

concept_cards.safe_claim: Vault deposits, withdrawals, and yield harvests are live on Arbitrum.

concept_cards.why_it_matters: Small, rule-bound operational funds — capped withdrawals on an interval, so everyday expenses don't need a treasury vote.
concept_cards.example: A gardener withdraws the weekly cap to buy seedlings.

not_confused_with.reason: jars are for frequent small spending; vaults are for principal that generates yield

concept_cards.safe_claim: Garden jars are provisioned automatically at garden mint; jar activity beyond creation is not yet indexed for reports.

concept_cards.why_it_matters: The permanence layer: every claim in Green Goods resolves to a signed, public, verifiable EAS record.
concept_cards.example: A Work attestation and its linked Work Approval, both inspectable on easscan.

not_confused_with.reason: a hypercert is a token bundling many attestations

concept_cards.safe_claim: Green Goods registers five EAS schemas on Arbitrum; core records are attested and publicly verifiable.

concept_cards.why_it_matters: Transparent, revocable authority: who may approve, submit, or assess is readable on-chain, not implied.
concept_cards.example: An operator hat lets its wearer approve work; revoking the hat removes the authority.

not_confused_with.reason: hats grant authority within a garden; they are not membership itself

concept_cards.safe_claim: Garden roles are live Hats Protocol tokens; the on-chain operator hat labels already read Steward.

concept_cards.why_it_matters: The shared clock of a garden — a bounded period that frames assessments, work, and harvest.
concept_cards.example: Season One: the current cohort of live gardens documenting work on Arbitrum.

not_confused_with.reason: a pool's Season cycle is the planned on-chain form of this same concept — one Season, two representations, not two Seasons

concept_cards.safe_claim: Seasons are a narrative frame today; the commitment-pooling Cycle gives them their first on-chain form.

concept_cards.why_it_matters: Gives a garden a shared, honest place for promises — offers and requests curated by the garden, capped per person.
concept_cards.example: A garden's pool holds an offer to teach a monthly workshop and a request to fix the fence.

not_confused_with.reason: a pool holds promises, never funds

concept_cards.safe_claim: Commitment pooling contracts are live and unpaused on Arbitrum with 18 pools registered; the in-app experience is still rolling out.

concept_cards.why_it_matters: Bounds a run of promises in time — a Season or a shorter campaign — so reconciliation has a clear close.
concept_cards.example: A garden seeds a Season cycle; its commitments reconcile when the cycle closes.

not_confused_with.reason: the Cycle of type Season is the on-chain representation of the garden's Season

concept_cards.safe_claim: Cycle mechanics are live at the contract layer; no user surface exists yet.

concept_cards.why_it_matters: A recorded promise — offer or request — with one accountable lead, evidence, and confirmation by someone other than the doer.
concept_cards.example: “I’ll water the beds while you’re away”, taken up, evidenced with a photo, confirmed by the recipient.

not_confused_with.reason: work documents what happened; the commitment is the promise it fulfills
commitments are module-native records, deliberately not EAS attestations

concept_cards.safe_claim: Commitments are live at the contract layer — a commitment is a record, never a coin: it cannot be traded, sold, or transferred.

concept_cards.why_it_matters: One durable identity for a repeated offer, so “I teach a workshop each month” is set up once and reused.
concept_cards.example: A monthly workshop offer paused over the holidays, then resumed.

not_confused_with.reason: a series is the durable identity; each instance is its own commitment

concept_cards.safe_claim: Series mechanics are live at the contract layer; the app surface is still rolling out.

concept_cards.why_it_matters: Names who helped on a promise; the roster freezes before confirmation so credit can't shift after the fact.
concept_cards.example: Three gardeners on a fence-repair commitment, frozen at readiness, each credited on fulfillment.

not_confused_with.reason: the roster is the per-commitment team; gardener is the garden-wide role

concept_cards.safe_claim: Roster and credit-freeze mechanics are live at the contract layer.

concept_cards.why_it_matters: Turns a fulfilled promise into a conserved, hash-bound payment split — every unit accounted for before anything moves.
concept_cards.example: A fulfilled campaign commitment finalizes one plan: garden share plus contributor payouts, summing exactly.

not_confused_with.reason: plans reference value; vaults custody it

concept_cards.safe_claim: Settlement contracts are deployed but paused; no value moves until the settlement authority activates.

concept_cards.why_it_matters: Lets a community write down what should change — a problem paired with a desired outcome — so promises and funding can answer it.
concept_cards.example: “The east beds flood every rain; we want working drainage”, later addressed by a fulfilled commitment.

not_confused_with.reason: a Need states the problem; the commitment that answers it carries the offer/request direction

concept_cards.safe_claim: Needs are a planned concept with locked architecture; nothing is deployed or user-visible yet.
